units.title: The London
units.kicker: White · one setup against the d-pawn
units.why: Bishop out before the e-pawn, then the king's knight, the c-pawn, the queen's knight and the light bishop. The same moves in the same order against nearly everything, and a trick for each of Black's usual tries.

idea.t: The dark bishop leaves before the e-pawn moves, so it is never shut in behind your own pawns.
E-pawn, king's knight, c-pawn, queen's knight beside the queen, light bishop, castle. Three pawns make a pyramid and both bishops stand outside it.
When Black's bishop comes opposite yours, keep yours. If Black takes it anyway, the h-pawn takes back and your rook already looks at Black's h-pawn.

idea.h: The queen raid on the b-pawn
idea.t: Your bishop has left the queenside, so the b-pawn has no guard. With the c-pawn already moved, your queen meets Black's and offers the trade.

idea.h: Bishop at your knight: queen at the b-pawn
idea.t: When Black's light bishop leaves for your knight, nothing guards Black's b-pawn either. Your queen hits it at once.

idea.h: The check that wins the knight
idea.t: Offer the light bishops and take back with the queen. If Black's knight jumps at her, the queen checks and hits the knight at the same time.

quiz.label: Bishop out first
quiz.note: The London bishop. It leaves before your e-pawn moves, so it is never shut in behind the pawns.

quiz.label: C-pawn one square
quiz.note: Now the d-pawn has a pawn behind it, whatever Black takes. The setup is a pyramid of pawns.

quiz.label: Step back and keep it
quiz.rule: Bishop opposite yours: step back, keep it
quiz.note: Your bishop stays on its diagonal. If Black takes it, your h-pawn takes back and your rook gets the h-file.

quiz.label: Queen out: offer the trade
quiz.rule: Queen at the b-pawn, c-pawn moved: offer the queens
quiz.note: Your c-pawn has already moved, so the queen can step out in front of the b-pawn. If Black trades, you take back toward the middle and your rook gets the a-file.

quiz.label: Queen hits the b-pawn
quiz.rule: Bishop left the b-pawn: the queen hits it
quiz.note: Black's light bishop used to guard it. Now Black has to spend a move on it.

quiz.label: Queen check
quiz.rule: Knight hits the queen: check, and take it
quiz.note: The check also hits the knight. Block with the pawn or the queen, and the knight falls; send the knight back to block, and the b-pawn falls.

units.title: The Italian
units.kicker: White · a big center aimed at f7
units.why: About one White game in eight goes into this line, and you have won only five of the last twelve. One idea runs through all of it: a big center, a quick castle, and every piece aimed at f7.

idea.t: Your bishop points at the pawn beside Black's king. Only the king defends it, and almost every trick in this unit lands there.

idea.h: Small pawn, then the big center
idea.t: The small c-pawn move prepares the d-pawn push. After the trade, two pawns stand side by side in the middle and kick Black's pieces around.
When Black grabs your e-pawn, don't defend anything. Castle: your rook comes to the open file while Black's king is still in the middle.
If Black's bishop keeps grabbing, your other bishop stops Black from ever castling. Let the corner rook go; the king pays for it.

quiz.label: A small pawn with a big plan
quiz.note: Push the c-pawn one square. It prepares the d-pawn push, so you can stand two pawns side by side in the center.

quiz.label: Strike the center
quiz.note: Push now. The pawn attacks Black's bishop and center pawn at the same time.

quiz.label: Block with the knight
quiz.rule: Block with the knight, offer the pawn
quiz.note: Block with the knight and offer your e-pawn. If Black takes it, you castle and attack while Black's king is still in the middle. The engine calls the gambit roughly equal, but Black has to find several exact moves to prove it.

quiz.label: Castle!
quiz.note: Castle and let Black keep the pawn. Your king is safe, your rook is about to use the open e-file, and Black's king is still in the middle. Black now has two ways to take your knight.

quiz.label: Bishop blocks castling
quiz.note: The key move. Don't save the rook. Your bishop now stops Black from ever castling, because the king would have to cross a square it attacks.

quiz.label: The Møller push
quiz.note: Push the d-pawn. It attacks Black's knight, and the bishop that took your knight can wait. This move is the heart of the whole line.

units.title: The Slav setup
units.kicker: Black · one setup against the d-pawn
units.why: A third of your Black games start with the d-pawn, and you have lost more of them than you have won. From now on it is one setup, in one order, every time: d-pawn, c-pawn, bishop out, then the e-pawn.

idea.t: Meet the d-pawn with yours and guard it with the c-pawn. The road for your light bishop stays open.

idea.h: Bishop out, then close the door
idea.t: The bishop leaves before the e-pawn moves. Then the three pawns make a triangle that is hard to attack, and the bishop is outside it.
King's knight, light bishop, e-pawn, queen's knight, dark bishop, castle. The pieces go to the same squares in every line, and when two move orders reach the same position your next move is the same.

If White plays the small e-pawn move before bringing a piece out, your bishop goes first and the king's knight waits until after the queen's knight. From home it leaves your queen guarding the edge square, so White's knight can't chase your bishop.

idea.h: When the e-pawn arrives, take it
idea.t: White's one active idea is the e-pawn push. Take it at once and trade knights. One square further and it would fork your bishop and knight.

idea.h: The same squares against the London
idea.t: Against the London the dark bishop comes out straight after the e-pawn and offers a trade. If White takes, the queen takes back, every time.
When the bishops come off and White's queen takes back, she can check your king and hit your b-pawn in one move. The c-pawn shuts that out, and it is the same triangle again.

quiz.label: Bishop out before the e-pawn
quiz.note: The one time the bishop goes before the king's knight. White has no piece out, so nothing can punish it, and if you wait White's bishop takes this diagonal first.

quiz.label: Queen's knight next
quiz.note: After the bishop and the e-pawn, the queen's knight always comes next. While your king's knight is at home your queen guards the edge square, so White's knight can't go there to chase your bishop.

quiz.label: Dark bishop to its square
quiz.note: The same square as in the first lesson, and the same position. Castle next. Equal: no weak pawns and no bad bishop.

quiz.label: Take back with the c-pawn
quiz.rule: Pawn trade: take back with the c-pawn
quiz.note: The position is symmetrical. Your knight will stand in front of the c-pawn's old square.

quiz.label: Offer the dark bishops
quiz.note: Against the London the dark bishop comes out before the queen's knight: it stands opposite the London bishop, and if White takes, the London player's favourite piece is gone.

quiz.label: C-pawn first
quiz.note: When White's queen takes back, the c-pawn goes before the e-pawn. It shuts out the queen check that would win your b-pawn, and it starts the same triangle as in the Slav.

units.title: The Caro-Kann
units.kicker: Black · a second answer to the e-pawn
units.why: Two pawn moves start every game: c-pawn one square, d-pawn two. Then the light bishop comes out before the e-pawn moves, the same idea as the Slav setup against the d-pawn.

idea.h: Two pawn moves in every game
idea.t: The c-pawn backs up the d-pawn, and the road for your light bishop stays open. Now White has to decide about the e-pawn: push it past, trade it, or guard it.

idea.h: Pushed past: bishop out, then hit the chain
idea.t: The bishop leaves before your e-pawn closes the door. Then the e-pawn one square, and the c-pawn two squares at the pawn that holds White's chain together.

idea.h: Traded: both knights before the bishop
idea.t: Take back with the c-pawn. With the c-pawns gone, White's queen can come out at your b-pawn the moment the bishop leaves, so the knights come first. The same rule as the Slav pawn trade.

idea.h: Guarded: take, then the bishop with a hit
idea.t: Take the e-pawn and bring the bishop out at the knight. When the knight steps aside and hits the bishop, step back one square and keep the diagonal.
Queen's knight, e-pawn, king's knight, dark bishop, castle. The queen's knight goes first because it covers the middle square White's knight wants.

idea.h: A free pawn in one game out of three
idea.t: A third of club players guard the knight with the bishop. That bishop now stands between White's queen and the d-pawn, so your queen takes it.

quiz.label: Bishop out first
quiz.note: The whole point of the opening: the bishop leaves before the e-pawn shuts the door. Then e-pawn, then the c-pawn two squares.

quiz.label: C-pawn two squares
quiz.note: It hits the pawn that holds White's chain together. Queen's knight behind it next.

quiz.label: King's knight
quiz.note: Both knights are out. Now the bishop can go.

quiz.label: Step back
quiz.rule: Step back, then the queen's knight
quiz.note: The bishop stays on its diagonal. From here the order is: queen's knight, e-pawn, king's knight.

quiz.label: Take the d-pawn
quiz.rule: Bishop guards the knight: take the d-pawn
quiz.note: The bishop stepped in front of the queen, so nothing guards it. A clean pawn.

quiz.label: Make room
quiz.rule: H-pawn comes: make room for the bishop
quiz.note: One square for the edge pawn gives the bishop a way back.

units.title: The Sicilian
units.kicker: Black · a third answer to the e-pawn
units.why: C-pawn two squares, e-pawn one, and take the d-pawn when it comes. After that the same moves in the same order: a-pawn, queen, king's knight, b-pawn.

idea.h: Two pawn moves in every game
idea.t: The c-pawn fights for the middle from the side. The e-pawn opens your bishop and shuts the road to f7.

idea.h: Take the d-pawn, then the a-pawn
idea.t: A side pawn for a middle pawn. The small a-pawn move keeps White's pieces off your queenside and gets the b-pawn ready.
The queen guards the middle square White's e-pawn wants. Only then the knight comes out, and then the b-pawn two squares.

idea.h: An early bishop runs into a wall
idea.t: One in six brings the bishop out on move two. Your e-pawn blocks it and the d-pawn hits it next move.
White wanted a big center. Meet it head on, then aim the knight and queen at the pawn that holds White's chain.

quiz.label: E-pawn one square
quiz.note: Always your second move. It opens the dark bishop and blunts any bishop that aims at f7.

quiz.label: A-pawn one square
quiz.note: The move that names the setup. No knight or bishop can land on the square beside it, and the b-pawn is ready to go two squares.

quiz.label: Queen beside the bishop
quiz.rule: Queen beside the bishop, then the knight
quiz.note: On the open file, guarding the middle square White's e-pawn wants to reach. It comes before the knight so that pawn push never arrives with a hit.

quiz.label: B-pawn hits the bishop
quiz.rule: Bishop comes out: b-pawn hits it
quiz.note: It has to move again, and your bishop gets the long diagonal with a hit on the e-pawn.

quiz.label: D-pawn hits the bishop
quiz.rule: Early bishop: e-pawn blocks, d-pawn hits
quiz.note: You take the middle and gain a move.

quiz.label: D-pawn two squares
quiz.note: Meet the center head on, before it is set.

units.title: The Dragon
units.kicker: Black · the Sicilian with the bishop on the long diagonal
units.why: C-pawn two squares, take the d-pawn when it comes, then one setup against everything: d-pawn one square, knight, g-pawn, bishop, castle. When White castles long, your rook takes the half-open file.

idea.h: Trade the d-pawn, then the g-pawn
idea.t: White pushes the d-pawn and you take it. Your knight makes White guard the e-pawn, and the g-pawn makes room for the bishop.

idea.h: Bishop to the long diagonal, then castle
idea.t: The bishop looks across the whole board at White's queenside. Castle behind it and the setup is done: the same moves against everything White tries.

idea.h: White castles long: the file is yours
idea.t: Your rook comes to the file the c-pawn opened. It points at White's king, and the knight heads for the middle to join in.

idea.h: No open game: the same first moves
idea.t: When White keeps the d-pawn back, nothing changes. D-pawn one square, knight, g-pawn, bishop: the setup comes out in its usual order.

quiz.label: The Dragon
quiz.rule: G-pawn, then the bishop to the long diagonal
quiz.note: The g-pawn makes room for the bishop. From the long diagonal it looks across the whole board at White's queenside.

quiz.label: Bishop to the long diagonal
quiz.rule: Bishop first; the knight jump waits
quiz.note: Bishop first, then castle. Your knight waits: jumping at White's bishop a move earlier would run into a bishop check.

quiz.label: Castle
quiz.note: King safe before the race starts.

quiz.label: Rook to the half-open file
quiz.rule: White castles long: rook to the half-open file
quiz.note: It looks straight down at White's king. The knight goes to the middle next.

quiz.label: Knight hits the queen
quiz.rule: Queen takes back: your knight hits her
quiz.note: She has to move again, and you have a piece out for free.

quiz.label: D-pawn one square
quiz.rule: Bishop out early: the same setup
quiz.note: The same first move. The bishop came out early, and your e-pawn can block it when it has to.

units.title: The Scandinavian
units.kicker: Black · the queen out and one setup
units.why: D-pawn two squares on move one. The queen takes back and steps to the side when the knight hits her; then knight, c-pawn, bishop and e-pawn come out in the same order every game.

idea.h: Queen out, then to the side
idea.t: White takes, your queen takes back, and the knight hits her. From the side she is out of reach, and the setup can start.
White's bishop lines up on your queen from behind the knight. The c-pawn move gives her a way back before the knight can jump.
Knight, c-pawn, bishop, e-pawn. The bishop is outside the pawns before the e-pawn moves, the same idea as in the Caro-Kann and the Slav.

idea.h: Pushed past: bishop out, then hit the chain
idea.t: When White won't take, your bishop leaves first, the e-pawn closes the door behind it, and the c-pawn hits the pawn that holds White's chain together.

quiz.label: Queen to the side
quiz.rule: Knight hits the queen: she steps to the side
quiz.note: Nothing can hit her here yet. Next comes the setup, in the same order every game: knight, c-pawn, bishop, e-pawn.

quiz.label: C-pawn one square
quiz.rule: C-pawn one square: a way home for the queen
quiz.note: The queen gets a way home, and White's knight loses its best square in the middle. Play it before the bishop comes out.

quiz.label: Bishop out
quiz.rule: Then the bishop out, then the e-pawn
quiz.note: Outside the pawns before the e-pawn moves, the same idea as in the Caro-Kann and the Slav.

quiz.label: Take the knight
quiz.note: Your queen was looking along the rank the whole time. A clean piece.

quiz.label: Bishop out first
quiz.rule: Pushed past: bishop out, then the c-pawn two squares
quiz.note: Before the e-pawn shuts it in. Then the e-pawn one square and the c-pawn two.

quiz.label: C-pawn two squares
quiz.note: It hits the pawn that holds White's chain together. The queen's knight comes behind it.

units.title: The French
units.kicker: Black · lock the middle and hit the chain
units.why: E-pawn one square, then the d-pawn two. When White pushes past, the middle is locked and your c-pawn, knight and queen go at the base of the chain; when White trades, your bishop is free.

idea.t: Your d-pawn hits the e-pawn, and the e-pawn behind it means it can't be pushed around. White has to push past, trade or guard.

idea.h: Hit the chain at its base
idea.t: The pushed pawn stands on the pawn behind it. That one is your target, and the c-pawn hits it straight away.
C-pawn, knight, queen. White's pieces are tied to the pawn, and the dark bishop can't leave home without dropping the pawn beside it.
When a knight guards the e-pawn, yours hits it. If the pawn pushes, the knight steps back and the c-pawn goes at the chain: the same plan.
When White trades, the line of your light bishop opens. Knight, bishop, castle, and the game is level.

quiz.label: D-pawn two squares
quiz.note: It hits the e-pawn. White has to push past, trade or guard it.

quiz.label: C-pawn hits the chain
quiz.rule: Pushed past: the c-pawn hits the chain
quiz.note: White's d-pawn holds the pushed pawn up. Hit the chain at its base.

quiz.label: Queen behind the c-pawn
quiz.rule: Knight, then the queen: three on one pawn
quiz.note: A third piece on the d-pawn, and she looks at the b-pawn too: White's dark bishop can't leave home without losing it.

quiz.label: E-pawn takes back
quiz.rule: Traded: e-pawn takes back, then knight and bishop
quiz.note: The light bishop has an open line now. Knight, bishop, castle.

quiz.label: Knight steps back
quiz.rule: Pushed: the knight steps back, then the c-pawn
quiz.note: It makes room for the f-pawn and backs up the c-pawn's push. The chain is on the board, and you know what to do with it.

quiz.label: D-pawn two squares
quiz.rule: Knight first: the d-pawn all the same
quiz.note: The same second move whatever White has played.

units.title: The Queen's Gambit Declined
units.kicker: Black · hold the middle and trade your way free
units.why: D-pawn two squares, and the e-pawn beside it when the c-pawn comes. Knight, bishop one square, castle; then the knight jumps into the middle and two pairs of pieces come off.

idea.t: White offers the c-pawn to pull your d-pawn away from the middle. The e-pawn steps up beside it, and the d-pawn stays where it is.
D-pawn, e-pawn, knight, bishop one square, castle. The bishop breaks the pin before it can hurt, and the king is safe.
The h-pawn asks the bishop first. Then the knight jumps in: your bishop and theirs come off, and so do the knights. With fewer pieces there is room for the ones that are left.

idea.h: Pawns traded: your bishop is free
idea.t: When White trades in the middle, the e-pawn takes back and the light bishop has an open line. The c-pawn makes the d-pawn safe for good.

quiz.label: E-pawn one square
quiz.rule: The gambit: e-pawn beside the d-pawn
quiz.note: You keep the pawn in the middle and say no to the gambit. The d-pawn is as safe as it gets.

quiz.label: Bishop one square
quiz.rule: Pinned: bishop one square, then castle
quiz.note: The pin is broken before it can hurt. You castle next.

quiz.label: H-pawn asks the bishop
quiz.note: It has to take or step back, and your king gets a square for later.

quiz.label: Knight jumps in
quiz.rule: Then the knight jumps in: two trades
quiz.note: It offers two trades at once: the bishops, and the knights. With fewer pieces your position has room.

quiz.label: E-pawn takes back
quiz.note: The line of your light bishop opens, and you keep a pawn in the middle.

quiz.label: C-pawn backs the d-pawn
quiz.rule: Then the c-pawn backs the d-pawn
quiz.note: The d-pawn can't be won now, and your queen has a diagonal.

units.title: The Queen's Gambit Declined against the London
units.kicker: Black · no gambit, so your c-pawn goes
units.why: The London, the Colle, the Jobava: White plays without the c-pawn. Nothing hits your d-pawn, so your own c-pawn goes two squares and your bishop offers a trade to White's best piece.

idea.t: The same two pawns as against the gambit. With nothing hitting your center, the c-pawn goes two squares at White's, and the knight comes out behind it.
It is White's best piece. If it takes, your queen takes back; if it steps away, you have gained a move and you castle.

idea.h: Knight first: your bishop comes out
idea.t: When White holds the c-pawn and the bishop back, your light bishop has time to come out. The e-pawn closes the door behind it.

quiz.label: E-pawn one square
quiz.rule: The London: e-pawn, then the c-pawn two squares
quiz.note: The same pawns as against the gambit. With no c-pawn hitting your center, yours goes two squares next.

quiz.label: C-pawn two squares
quiz.note: It hits the d-pawn, and the knight comes out behind it.

quiz.label: Bishop offers a trade
quiz.rule: Offer the London bishop a trade
quiz.note: The London bishop is White's best piece. If it takes, your queen takes back and stands well; if it steps back, you castle.

quiz.label: Bishop out before White's bishop
quiz.note: Get it out now. Once White's bishop reaches the middle square, yours would be stuck behind the e-pawn.

units.title: The King's Indian
units.kicker: Black · five moves before the e-pawn
units.why: Knight, g-pawn, bishop, d-pawn, castle: the same five moves against every d-pawn system. Then the e-pawn strikes at the center White has built.

idea.t: The bishop goes to the long diagonal, behind your own pawns for now. White is welcome to the center: you will hit it later.
The d-pawn keeps White's e-pawn from pushing at your knight. Then the king is safe, and the setup is complete: five moves, always in this order.
Two squares, at the d-pawn, with your bishop behind it. If White trades pawns and queens you lose nothing, and your pieces come out with gain of time.

idea.h: Middle closed? Play on the wings
idea.t: When White pushes past, your knight takes the square in front of the c-pawn and hits the e-pawn. The a-pawn keeps it there, and the f-pawn is your attack.

quiz.label: G-pawn one square
quiz.note: It makes room for the bishop on the long diagonal.

quiz.label: Bishop to the long diagonal
quiz.note: It looks through the middle at White's d-pawn. Everything you do later is about opening this diagonal.

quiz.label: D-pawn one square
quiz.rule: Big center: d-pawn one square, then castle
quiz.note: It keeps White's e-pawn from pushing on at your knight, and gets your own e-pawn ready.

quiz.label: Castle
quiz.note: King safe before the middle opens.

quiz.label: E-pawn two squares
quiz.note: The strike the whole setup was built for.

quiz.label: Castle
quiz.rule: Four pawns: castle, then the e-pawn
quiz.note: Let White build. Your e-pawn hits the wall next.

units.title: The King's Indian against the London
units.kicker: Black · the same five moves
units.why: The London, the Torre, the Colle, the Trompowsky: White plays without the c-pawn. Your setup doesn't change, and two details are worth knowing.

idea.t: Five moves, the same order. Next a knight goes behind the e-pawn and it pushes two squares, with a gain of time on the London bishop.

idea.h: Queen's knight first? D-pawn two squares
idea.t: White wants the e-pawn in the middle next. This is the one time your d-pawn goes two: the e-pawn can no longer walk in for free, and your light bishop comes out.

idea.h: Bishop takes your knight? E-pawn takes back
idea.t: Carry on with the g-pawn. If the bishop takes, take back toward the middle: you have both bishops and an open file for the rook.

quiz.label: G-pawn one square
quiz.rule: London bishop: the same five moves
quiz.note: The same setup against the London. Your bishop will look straight down the long diagonal.

quiz.label: D-pawn two squares
quiz.rule: Queen's knight on move two: d-pawn two squares
quiz.note: The one time the d-pawn goes two. White's e-pawn can no longer walk into the middle for free.

quiz.label: E-pawn takes back
quiz.rule: Bishop takes your knight: e-pawn takes back
quiz.note: Toward the middle. You have the two bishops and an open file for the rook.

units.title: Spot the threat
units.kicker: Skill · from your own games
units.why: In 23 of your last 28 losses there was at least one moment like this: a piece left hanging, or a threat you didn't look for. Every position here is from your own games, at the moment it went wrong.

idea.h: What did their last move attack?
idea.t: Before you touch a piece, look at the move your opponent just made and everything it now hits. Here the knight attacked your queen.

idea.h: Can my piece be taken where it lands?
idea.t: Then check your own move. Here the queen had to move, and it went to a square a knight covered (blue: your move, red: the reply).
Last, look at every check your opponent has. Here the new queen didn't matter: the checks came first, and they ended the game.

units.title: Against the Italian
units.kicker: Black · your one e-pawn setup
units.why: Your best e-pawn opening as Black: ten wins in fifteen games. It is also the home of the setup you will use everywhere: knight out, bishop to its diagonal, castle.

idea.t: Your bishop goes to the same kind of diagonal as White's and aims at f2, the pawn beside White's king.
When White pushes the d-pawn, take it, then check with the bishop. Stepping back would give the pawns time to roll.
After the bishops come off, your d-pawn hits the center before White's pawns can advance.
Your rook now guards f7 and your king has stepped away. Next the h-pawn kicks the knight back home.

quiz.label: Mirror the bishop
quiz.note: Your bishop goes to the same diagonal and aims at f2.

quiz.label: Bishop check
quiz.note: Check first, then trade bishops. Retreating gives the center time to roll.

quiz.label: The d-pawn strikes
quiz.note: The point of the whole line: hit the center before White's pawns can roll. It hits the bishop too.

quiz.label: Knight grabs the e-pawn
quiz.note: Take it. Your knight also hits the knight that blocks the check.

quiz.label: Small d-pawn move
quiz.note: Your e-pawn is guarded for good. Same setup every time.

quiz.label: Castle
quiz.note: Your rook now guards f7 and your king is out of the line of fire.

units.title: The Ruy Lopez
units.kicker: White · lean on the knight, then take the middle
units.why: The bishop comes at the knight that guards Black's e-pawn, and steps back when a pawn asks. Then castle, rook, c-pawn, the small h-pawn and the d-pawn two squares: one setup, the most played in the history of the game.

idea.t: The knight is all that guards Black's e-pawn, and your bishop looks straight at it. Nothing is won yet, but Black has to mind it on every move.

idea.h: Two steps back, one good diagonal
idea.t: A pawn asks the bishop and it steps back; a second pawn asks and it steps back again. It ends on the diagonal at f7, and Black's wing pawns have moved forward for nothing.
You can castle with the e-pawn hanging: if the knight takes it, the rook comes to the open file in front of Black's king. Once the rook stands there, the pawn is guarded for good.
The c-pawn backs the d-pawn up, and the small h-pawn move keeps Black's bishop from pinning your knight. Now the d-pawn goes two squares.

idea.h: The small d-pawn: open the middle
idea.t: Black's d-pawn guards the e-pawn but leaves the knight pinned to the king. Hit the e-pawn at once, while the knight can't move.

quiz.label: Bishop comes at the knight
quiz.rule: The bishop comes at the knight
quiz.note: That knight guards the e-pawn. Nothing is threatened yet, but every move Black makes has to keep it in mind.

quiz.label: Bishop steps back
quiz.rule: A pawn asks: the bishop steps back
quiz.note: It still looks at the knight. Taking it would give up the bishop for little.

quiz.label: Bishop steps back again
quiz.rule: A second pawn: back again, to the diagonal at f7
quiz.note: Now it stands on the diagonal at f7, and Black's pawns on the wing have moved forward for nothing.

quiz.label: Castle
quiz.rule: Castle; the e-pawn can be left
quiz.note: The e-pawn can be left: if the knight takes it, the rook comes to the open file in front of Black's king.

quiz.label: Castle
quiz.rule: Knight hits the e-pawn: castle anyway
quiz.note: Leave the e-pawn. If the knight takes it, your rook or your d-pawn opens the middle in front of Black's king.

quiz.label: D-pawn two squares
quiz.rule: The small d-pawn: open the middle at once
quiz.note: The d-pawn move left the knight pinned to the king. Open the middle while it can't move.

units.title: The slow Italian
units.kicker: White · one setup, no early fight
units.why: The Italian bishop, then two small pawn moves, castle, rook, and the knight goes round to the kingside. The same order against the bishop, the knight and almost everything else.

idea.t: Knight, knight, bishop: the Italian starts the same way. The bishop aims at f7, the pawn only the king guards.
The d-pawn guards the e-pawn, and the c-pawn takes the middle squares from Black's knight. Nothing is traded yet and nothing can go wrong early.

idea.h: Castle, rook, and the knight goes round
idea.t: The rook stands behind the e-pawn, and the queen's knight heads past it to the kingside, where your attack will be.

quiz.label: Bishop aims at f7
quiz.rule: The Italian bishop, aimed at f7
quiz.note: The Italian bishop. It aims at f7, the one pawn that only Black's king protects. Almost every trick in your book lands on that square.

quiz.label: Small d-pawn move
quiz.rule: Small d-pawn move, then the c-pawn
quiz.note: One square, not two. It guards the e-pawn, and nothing gets traded early.

quiz.label: Small c-pawn move
quiz.note: It keeps Black's knight out of the middle and gives your bishop a way back. The d-pawn can go forward later, when everything is ready.

quiz.label: Castle
quiz.rule: Castle, then the rook beside the king
quiz.note: King safe. The rook comes beside it next.

quiz.label: D-pawn guards the e-pawn
quiz.rule: Knight hits the e-pawn: the d-pawn guards it
quiz.note: No knight jump is needed. The setup carries on, and it usually runs into the same positions as against the bishop.

quiz.label: Trade knights
quiz.rule: Knight jumps in: trade, never grab
quiz.note: Simple and good. Don't take the center pawn.

units.title: The Sicilian
units.kicker: White · same plan as your Italian
units.why: About one White game in seven, and you have lost more of them than you have won. The plan is your Italian plan: the small c-pawn move, then the big center.

idea.t: As in your Italian, the c-pawn gets ready for the d-pawn push. Two pawns in the middle are coming.

idea.h: A knight in front of your pawn? Push it
idea.t: Black's knight stands where your d-pawn can hit it. Push, then push again with the f-pawn and the e-pawn.

idea.h: Push the knights off the board
idea.t: Every pawn push kicks a knight. Black's pieces run out of squares.
If the queen grabs your d-pawn, take the knight with check first. When the pawn takes back, your queen takes Black's.

quiz.label: Alapin Variation
quiz.rule: Small pawn move, like the Italian
quiz.note: The same idea as your Italian: get ready to push the d-pawn and stand two pawns in the center.

quiz.label: Push past the knight
quiz.rule: Knight in front of your pawn? Push it
quiz.note: Kick the knight out of the center. You skipped this against three opponents.

quiz.label: Kick it again
quiz.note: Your f-pawn chases the knight. It is running out of squares.

quiz.label: Now the other knight
quiz.note: Push again and hit Black's other knight. Black's pieces are being pushed off the board.

quiz.label: Take the knight with check
quiz.note: Check first. When the pawn takes back, Black's queen has no defender.

units.title: The Open Sicilian
units.kicker: White · one setup, then the pawns
units.why: Knight out, d-pawn two squares, the knight takes back. Then the same moves against every Sicilian: queen's knight, f-pawn, bishop, queen, castle long, and the g-pawn goes at Black's king.

idea.h: Open the middle, take back with the knight
idea.t: Your d-pawn goes two squares and Black trades it off. The knight takes back and stands in the middle of the board, and the queen's knight guards the e-pawn.
The f-pawn guards the e-pawn and keeps Black's knight from jumping at your bishop. The bishop sits beside the queen, and the king is ready to castle long.
Your king has gone the other way, so the pawns in front of Black's king are free to run. The g-pawn pushes the knight off its post first.

idea.h: When the e-pawn hits the knight
idea.t: Black's e-pawn has left a hole behind it. Here the square in front of the knight is free, so it jumps forward and heads for that hole. When Black's a-pawn guards the square, the knight steps back toward the queenside instead.

quiz.label: Knight out
quiz.rule: Knight out, then the d-pawn two squares
quiz.note: The d-pawn goes two squares next, and this knight takes back when Black trades it.

quiz.label: Knight takes back
quiz.note: It stands in the middle of the board, and nothing can chase it yet.

quiz.label: F-pawn one square
quiz.rule: F-pawn one square, then bishop and queen
quiz.note: It guards the e-pawn a second time and keeps Black's knight from jumping at the bishop that comes next.

quiz.label: Castle long
quiz.note: The kings are on opposite wings, so your kingside pawns are free to run.

quiz.label: Knight jumps forward
quiz.rule: E-pawn hits the knight: jump forward
quiz.note: The square in front is free, and Black's e-pawn has left a hole behind it. The knight is headed there.

quiz.label: Bishop out before the f-pawn
quiz.rule: Accelerated Dragon: bishop out before the f-pawn
quiz.note: Black saved a move with the d-pawn to push it two squares in one go. Your bishop stops that first.

units.title: The London against the Indian Defense
units.kicker: White · the same bishop against the knight
units.why: Against the king's knight the bishop still comes out on move two. Against the fianchetto two small changes keep it safe; against the e-pawn and the d-pawn you are back in the setup.

idea.h: The same bishop and the same move
idea.t: The knight changes nothing on move two. The setup comes out as usual unless Black puts the dark bishop behind the g-pawn.

idea.h: Against the fianchetto: a way back
idea.t: The light bishop goes one square instead of two, out of reach of a pawn fork. The h-pawn makes a way back for the London bishop before Black can hit it.

idea.h: The e-pawn push costs a pawn
idea.t: Black's usual plan is to push the e-pawn at your bishop. Take it, and when Black takes back, two of your pieces hit the pawn and only one guards it.

idea.h: The e-pawn and the d-pawn: home again
idea.t: Four club players in ten answer with the e-pawn or the d-pawn, and the moves walk straight back into the setup you already know.

quiz.label: Bishop out first
quiz.note: Same move as against the d-pawn.

quiz.label: Light bishop one square
quiz.note: Not two squares: there Black's e-pawn could come forward and fork it with your knight. One square back it stays out of the way.

quiz.label: H-pawn one square
quiz.rule: D-pawn one square: make a way back for the bishop
quiz.note: Now your bishop has a way back when it is hit.

quiz.label: Bishop steps back
quiz.note: This is what the h-pawn move was for. Your bishop keeps its diagonal.

quiz.label: Take it
quiz.note: Your d-pawn takes, and Black has to take back.

quiz.label: Take back with the e-pawn
quiz.note: Same rule as in the setup.

units.title: Scotch & center gambits
units.kicker: Black · the same bishop on the same diagonal
units.why: Thirteen games and only four wins: your weakest Black opening. Now it is your Italian setup: the bishop goes straight to its diagonal, the queen joins it against f2, and against the gambits you develop instead of grabbing a second pawn.

idea.t: When White takes back with the knight, your bishop goes straight to its Italian diagonal. It hits the knight in the middle and aims at f2. A check first only costs a move.

idea.h: Knight trade? The queen joins in
idea.t: Queen and bishop both hit f2 and mate is threatened. White has to spend a move on it; then your d-pawn takes back toward the middle and you castle long.
Taking the second pawn lets White's bishop take on f7 and the queen win your bishop back with check. It happened twice. Bring the knight out and you are in your Italian.
Don't take the second pawn here either. The d-pawn strike opens the center for your pieces and leaves White with a lone pawn in the middle.

quiz.label: Bishop to its diagonal
quiz.note: The same square as in your Italian. It hits the knight in the middle and aims at f2. Don't check first: the bishop ends up here anyway, a move later.

quiz.label: Queen hits f2
quiz.note: Queen and bishop both aim at f2: mate is threatened. White has to deal with it before anything else.

quiz.label: D-pawn takes back
quiz.note: Toward the middle: your other bishop gets its road and the d-file opens for your rook.

quiz.label: Queen joins in
quiz.note: Now the knight in the middle is hit three times.

quiz.label: Knight out, not the second pawn
quiz.rule: Develop, don't take a second pawn
quiz.note: Develop. Taking the c-pawn walks into the bishop sacrifice on f7, as against themobun.

quiz.label: The d-pawn strikes
quiz.rule: Danish: hit back with the d-pawn
quiz.note: Don't take the second pawn. Hit back in the center. Against yonatha32 you took it and White's pieces came out with tempo.

units.title: The Caro-Kann
units.kicker: White · two lines cover most games
units.why: About one White game in seven, and you win two in three. Two lines cover most of them: the h-pawn march and the knight trade.

idea.t: Black's bishop comes out early. Your knight steps back and attacks it.
The pawn threatens to trap the bishop. Later it cramps Black's whole kingside.
Swap off Black's best piece, put your king on the other side, and attack where your h-pawn already stands.
Taking with check spoils Black's pawns. Stepping back, as you did in your games, gave Black an easy game.

quiz.label: Knight guards the pawn
quiz.note: Defend with a piece. You played this in all 13 games; keep doing it.

quiz.label: Knight hits the bishop
quiz.note: Step back with tempo. The bishop must move again.

quiz.label: Push the h-pawn at the bishop
quiz.rule: Push the h-pawn at the bishop
quiz.note: The pawn threatens to keep going and trap the bishop. Black has to answer it.

quiz.label: Pawn forward again
quiz.note: Kick the bishop to the edge. Your pawn now cramps Black's whole kingside.

quiz.label: Offer the bishop trade
quiz.note: Your bishop meets Black's best piece. Trading it leaves Black passive.

quiz.label: Take the knight
quiz.note: Trade with check. Black has to take back with a pawn and spoil the pawn structure. Your old move, stepping back, gave Black an easy game.

units.title: The Caro-Kann: push past
units.kicker: White · space for good
units.why: When Black's d-pawn meets yours, the e-pawn steps past it. Then knight, bishop one square and castle, and the c-pawn backs the chain when Black hits it.

idea.t: Black's d-pawn came to trade. The e-pawn steps past it instead, and the two pawns in the middle take room from Black for the rest of the game.
No hurry and no tricks. The bishop sits one square out, where Black's bishop can't bother it, and you castle next.
Black hits the base of your chain. The c-pawn holds it, and when the pawns are traded your knight takes back with a hit on the bishop.

quiz.label: Push past
quiz.rule: The d-pawn meets yours: push past
quiz.note: The e-pawn steps past instead of trading. The two pawns take room from Black for the rest of the game.

quiz.label: Knight out
quiz.rule: Knight, then the bishop one square, then castle
quiz.note: Let the bishop sit there. Knight, then the bishop one square, then castle.

quiz.label: Bishop one square
quiz.note: Out of the way and out of reach. You castle next.

quiz.label: Castle
quiz.note: King safe first. The c-pawn backs up the chain on the next move.

quiz.label: C-pawn backs the chain
quiz.rule: C-pawn hits the chain: yours backs it
quiz.note: Black is hitting the base of your chain. If the pawns are traded there, another pawn stands in the same place.

quiz.label: Knight takes back
quiz.rule: Pawns traded: the knight takes back
quiz.note: It lands in the middle with a hit on the bishop, and the c-pawn still keeps Black's knight out of the squares in front of it.

units.title: The London: other first moves
units.kicker: White · the same setup against anything
units.why: Most other first moves lead back to the setup. Two need something new: the c-pawn two squares, where your d-pawn pushes past it, and the e-pawn gambit, where one move avoids a famous trap.

idea.h: Most roads lead to the setup
idea.t: The e-pawn first, the c-pawn one square, the b-pawn or the f-pawn: your bishop comes out and the same moves follow.

idea.h: The gambit: the knight, never the bishop
idea.t: Take the pawn and guard it. When Black's queen takes your b-pawn, the knight comes out. The bishop to the same square loses to a mate in the corner.

idea.h: The c-pawn two squares: push past it
idea.t: Bringing the bishop out first would leave the b-pawn to Black's queen. Push the d-pawn past, then the knight and the e-pawn take the middle.

quiz.label: Take it
quiz.note: A free pawn. Keep it if you can do so safely.

quiz.label: Block with the bishop
quiz.note: The usual block. Black's queen takes the b-pawn next.

quiz.label: Knight out
quiz.rule: Queen takes the b-pawn: the knight, never the bishop
quiz.note: Now your queen guards the corner rook and the knight guards the a-pawn. Never the bishop to the same square: that is the trap.

quiz.label: Push past it
quiz.rule: C-pawn two squares: push past it
quiz.note: The d-pawn gains space. Bringing the bishop out first would leave the b-pawn to Black's queen.

quiz.label: Knight out
quiz.note: It guards the pawn and gets ready for the e-pawn.

quiz.label: Take back with the e-pawn
quiz.note: As always.

units.title: The English
units.kicker: White · one wedge for one square
units.why: C-pawn, queen's knight, g-pawn, bishop: four moves that aim at one light square. Then the e-pawn, the knight behind it, castle and the small d-pawn move. One rule on top: when Black's d-pawn comes two squares, take it.

idea.h: Three men aimed at one square
idea.t: C-pawn, knight, g-pawn, bishop: four moves, always in this order. Pawn, knight and bishop all aim at the same light square in the middle.
E-pawn two squares, king's knight tucked in behind it, castle, small d-pawn move. Eight moves, and Black's d-pawn can no longer come forward without being taken.
The one rule on top of the setup. After the trade your bishop's diagonal opens all the way, the e-pawn stays home and the king's knight comes out in front of the f-pawn.
When Black's bishop comes out to your knight and the d-pawn then moves, the queen checks and hits the bishop at once. One in fourteen club players walks into it.
One in five jumps a knight in beside the bishop. The small e-pawn move shuts the bishop out, and your queen looks at the knight.

quiz.label: Queen's knight out
quiz.rule: Queen's knight, then the g-pawn and the bishop
quiz.note: The second move of the setup, whatever Black plays. Knight and c-pawn watch the same light square in the middle.

quiz.label: G-pawn one square
quiz.note: It makes room for the bishop on the long diagonal.

quiz.label: E-pawn two squares
quiz.rule: Bishop on its diagonal: now the e-pawn two squares
quiz.note: A fourth guard for the light square in the middle. The dark square in front of your d-pawn is the price, and your knight will cover it from behind the e-pawn.

quiz.label: Take it
quiz.rule: D-pawn comes two squares: take it
quiz.note: The rule against the d-pawn: take it. Your bishop's diagonal will be open all the way.

quiz.label: Queen check
quiz.rule: Loose bishop, d-pawn moved: queen check wins it
quiz.note: The bishop has no guard, and the check hits it too. Black can block with the knight to guard it, but your bishop takes that knight.

quiz.label: Small e-pawn move
quiz.rule: Knight and bishop at f2: small e-pawn move
quiz.note: Knight and bishop both aim at f2. One square shuts the bishop out, and your queen now looks at the knight.

units.title: The English: Black copies or waits
units.kicker: White · the same eight moves
units.why: The c-pawn against yours, or a knight and a fianchetto first. Your order doesn't change, and the d-pawn push is what ends the symmetry.

idea.t: C-pawn against c-pawn, fianchetto against fianchetto. Your order stays the same: the e-pawn goes two squares and the knight tucks in behind it.
With the setup done, the bishop comes out to look at the c-pawn and your d-pawn goes two squares. Whoever gets that push in first has the easier game.

idea.h: Against the fianchetto: all eight moves
idea.t: One in three who start with the knight fianchetto next. Nothing changes: wedge, knight behind it, castle.

idea.h: The e-pawn one square: knight first
idea.t: Black gets ready for the d-pawn push, and the wedge would be too slow. The king's knight comes out in front of the f-pawn, and when the d-pawn comes, you take it.

quiz.label: E-pawn two squares
quiz.note: The same wedge against the mirror setup.

quiz.label: King's knight out
quiz.note: Black's e-pawn has gone one square to back up the d-pawn. The wedge would be too slow, so the knight comes out the usual way, and the d-pawn is taken when it arrives.

units.title: The English: the d-pawn and rare moves
units.kicker: White · take it
units.why: Black's d-pawn comes two squares, at once or backed up by a pawn. Take it every time. With the c-pawn gone, your d-pawn and e-pawn take the middle instead of the wedge.

idea.t: Nine in ten take back with the queen. Your knight comes out with an attack on her, and she has to move again.

idea.h: Without the c-pawn there is no wedge
idea.t: With the c-pawn traded off and Black's queen back home, the d-pawn and the e-pawn take the whole middle.
Four in ten castle here. The e-pawn pushes at the knight, and once it leaves the king your bishop takes the h-pawn with check.
The one time the g-pawn stays home: Black's bishop already owns the long diagonal. Pawns in the middle shut it out.

quiz.label: Take it
quiz.rule: D-pawn at once: take it, then the knight hits the queen
quiz.note: The rule against the d-pawn, on move two as well.

quiz.label: Knight out
quiz.note: The queen has to move again, and you are a move ahead.

quiz.label: D-pawn two squares
quiz.note: Without the c-pawn there is no wedge. With Black's queen back home, take the whole middle instead.

quiz.label: D-pawn two squares
quiz.note: After the trade Black has a pawn fixed in the middle. Put yours beside it; the dark bishop comes out next.

quiz.label: D-pawn two squares
quiz.rule: Bishop owns the long diagonal: pawns in the middle
quiz.note: Black's bishop already owns the long diagonal, so your own g-pawn move would lose the corner rook. Take the middle with pawns instead.

units.title: Against the Ruy Lopez
units.kicker: Black · the same setup against a new bishop
units.why: The same setup as your Italian: hit the e-pawn with the knight, bishop to its diagonal, castle. You have won seven of ten here.

idea.t: Your knight attacks White's center pawn at once.

idea.h: Bishop out, as in the Italian
idea.t: Same diagonal, aimed at f2. Castle next.
After the bishop takes your knight, take back with the d-pawn. If the knight grabs your pawn, your queen hits the knight and the e-pawn at once.

quiz.label: Knight hits the e-pawn
quiz.note: The Berlin. Go after White's e-pawn at once.

quiz.label: Bishop out, as in the Italian
quiz.rule: White castled: bishop out, as in the Italian
quiz.note: Same diagonal as in your Italian, aimed at f2. Castle next.

quiz.label: Bishop steps back
quiz.note: It keeps its diagonal toward White's king. About equal: White has more center, you have easy development.

quiz.label: Bishop to the Italian diagonal
quiz.note: Same square as in your Italian, aimed at f2. You won both games where you played it.

quiz.label: Take toward the center
quiz.note: Your queen and bishop open up at once. Against vasylsaienko the b-pawn took and your bishop was lost four moves later.

quiz.label: Queen fork
quiz.note: Your queen hits the knight and the e-pawn.

units.title: Finish the job
units.kicker: Skill · from your own games

units.title: Vienna & early attacks

Now the bishop goes to its usual diagonal and aims at f2. It is your Italian setup with the knights already out.
Against the f-pawn gambits your bishop takes the diagonal White's king needs. White can't castle short, and grabbing your e-pawn opens the king up.
If the f-pawn grabs your e-pawn, the queen checks, then takes the e-pawn with check and hits the rook in the corner.
